criteria.name: Identity and source-backed footprint
criteria.evidence: Recognizable Purdue Memorial Union tower-and-wing plan. Historic Purdue Libraries GIS and the earlier independent baseline support the main shell footprint; 18 original named wall/base bounds are unchanged within 1 mm. GIS phases are historic and approximate.

criteria.name: Placement, orientation, and scale
criteria.evidence: Read-only master inspection documented one PMU marker at (205.75, -271.65, 0), zero rotation, and unit scale. The individual asset root remains at identity. No current master write/reopen was performed as part of this isolated asset grade.

criteria.name: Height, floors, and roof transitions
criteria.evidence: The model has a taller central tower and pitched wing-roof additions, but 29.5 m total height, floor spacing, and roof elevations are explicitly estimates. Independent south, west, and roof views show broad roof planes dominating the mass, abrupt/awkward overlaps and cutouts, and weak tower-to-wing transitions. The sources are photographs, not measured elevations.

criteria.name: Facade rhythm, entrance, and distinctive details
criteria.evidence: R1 improves on the baseline with six arched wing windows, archivolts, a glazed arched entry, and an upper tower surround. Against the Purdue 1924 and 2024 photos, the wings remain repetitive and underspecified; the portal, relief fields, and tower glazing are schematic, the upper glazing lacks the reference's full composition, and the roof mass obscures/readably competes with the facade.

criteria.name: Modular portability and evidence/validation
criteria.evidence: Builder source, provenance notes, fresh-reopen validation, assigned materials, and no external image dependencies are supplied. I independently reopened the saved asset and verified SHA-256 9f3d804155efb70e13ba49706f7da88f61a93a30f981612ec318eca2f3cac0f6, root identity, and portability. Deduction: validation_r1.json compares to .blend1, but the current .blend1 is a prior R1 save rather than the original baseline; independent original-baseline comparison supports 18 unchanged wall/base bounds, not 21 preserved original bounds. Three current wall/base pieces are additive.

limitations: The official historic GIS supports footprint and phase context only, not current elevation, detailed facade geometry, interior layout, or roof dimensions.
The 1924 archival photo and 2024 Purdue photo depict different dates and perspectives; facade comparisons are qualitative.
Master placement was read from prior read-only evidence and not modified or freshly written during this review.

Visual review renders were independently produced from the saved asset with review lighting; their pale slate appearance may be lighting-driven, but large roof forms and transitions remain geometrically simplified.
actionable_findings: Rebuild roof masses as separate, lower-profile slate wing roofs with clear eaves, ridges, valleys, and controlled intersections; the current broad surfaces overpower the facade and look like a canopy.

Use a source-matched south elevation to refine the tower's multi-level glazed composition and the wing opening rhythm; reduce repeated rectangular side-wall fenestration where current imagery supports a more specific pattern.
Refine the main portal scale and stone surround and add only photo-supported relief/statue geometry; current entry is recognizable but schematic.
Keep height/floor claims labeled as estimates unless measured elevation data is added.

Correct validation provenance: retain an immutable pre-edit baseline or compare directly against the audited original hash and structural-bounds record; distinguish 18 unchanged original wall/base bounds from 3 added base pieces.
